database_summary: Small mixed-domain SQLite schema containing (a) hardware/product/customer dimension and monthly sales facts with related price/cost/deduction facts (typical star schema), (b) a modest web CRM dataset (accounts, events, sales reps, regions, orders), (c) a small university academic dataset (students, faculty, offerings, enrollment, courses), and (d) several heterogeneous example tables (StaffHours, SalaryDataset). The largest table is hardware_fact_sales_monthly (event/measurement, ~971k rows). Many tables are descriptive dimensions or small reference lists. Use caution when joining fact tables to dimension tables because the monthly sales fact will multiply when joined to other facts without aggregation.

accepted.name: hardware_sales_monthly_clean
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  date AS date,
  product_code AS product_code,
  customer_code AS customer_code,
  COALESCE(sold_quantity,0) AS sold_quantity,
  fiscal_year AS fiscal_year
FROM hardware_fact_sales_monthly
accepted.description: Normalized/cleaned monthly hardware sales fact. Parses/normalizes the date to ISO YYYY-MM-DD (keeps as TEXT), ensures numeric sold_quantity and fiscal_year are preserved. Use this as the canonical monthly sales input to downstream joins/aggregations to avoid repeated casts or NULL surprises. | Use for: monthly sales trends for a product/customer/market; aggregate sold_quantity by year/quarter/month; join to price/cost/discount by fiscal_year

accepted.name: hardware_product_master
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_code AS product_code,
  division AS division,
  segment AS segment,
  category AS category,
  product AS product,
  variant AS variant
FROM hardware_dim_product
accepted.description: Canonical product dimension pass-through. Use when analyses need product descriptive attributes (division, segment, category, product, variant) keyed by product_code. | Use for: product-level rollups (by division/segment/category); enrich sales with product attributes

accepted.name: hardware_customer_master
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_code AS customer_code,
  customer AS customer,
  platform AS platform,
  channel AS channel,
  market AS market,
  sub_zone AS sub_zone,
  region AS region
FROM hardware_dim_customer
accepted.description: Canonical customer dimension pass-through. Use when analyses need customer descriptive attributes keyed by customer_code. | Use for: sales by market/platform/channel/region; customer-level aggregation and segmentation

accepted.name: hardware_prices_by_year
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_code AS product_code,
  fiscal_year AS fiscal_year,
  gross_price AS gross_price
FROM hardware_fact_gross_price
accepted.description: Canonical gross price per product per fiscal_year. Use when joining yearly price data to sales aggregated to fiscal year or otherwise aligning by year. | Use for: compute revenue using gross_price and sold quantities aggregated by year; price trend analysis by product

accepted.name: hardware_costs_by_year
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_code AS product_code,
  cost_year AS cost_year,
  manufacturing_cost AS manufacturing_cost
FROM hardware_fact_manufacturing_cost
accepted.description: Canonical manufacturing cost per product per cost_year. Use when aligning manufacturing_cost to sales aggregated by year. | Use for: compute margin using manufacturing cost and revenue by year; cost trend analysis by product

accepted.name: hardware_customer_deductions_by_year
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_code AS customer_code,
  fiscal_year AS fiscal_year,
  pre_invoice_discount_pct AS pre_invoice_discount_pct
FROM hardware_fact_pre_invoice_deductions
accepted.description: Canonical pre-invoice deduction percentage per customer per fiscal_year. Use to apply discounts when aggregating sales to year/customer. | Use for: apply customer discounts to yearly revenue calculations; analyze discount rates by customer and year

accepted.name: sales_monthly_enriched
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.date AS date,
  s.product_code AS product_code,
  s.customer_code AS customer_code,
  s.sold_quantity AS sold_quantity,
  s.fiscal_year AS fiscal_year,
  p.division AS division,
  p.segment AS segment,
  p.category AS category,
  p.product AS product,
  p.variant AS variant,
  c.customer AS customer,
  c.platform AS platform,
  c.channel AS channel,
  c.market AS market,
  c.sub_zone AS sub_zone,
  c.region AS region
FROM hardware_sales_monthly_clean AS s
LEFT JOIN hardware_dim_product AS p ON s.product_code = p.product_code
LEFT JOIN hardware_dim_customer AS c ON s.customer_code = c.customer_code
accepted.description: Monthly sales enriched with product and customer descriptive attributes. Keeps sales grain (one row per date/product_code/customer_code) and preserves keys for further aggregation. | Use for: sales by product attributes (category/segment/division); sales by customer geography/market/channel; pivoting monthly sales to higher-level groupings

accepted.name: monthly_sales_by_product_year
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_code AS product_code,
  fiscal_year AS fiscal_year,
  SUM(sold_quantity) AS total_sold_quantity
FROM hardware_sales_monthly_clean
GROUP BY product_code, fiscal_year
accepted.description: Aggregated sold_quantity per product per fiscal_year. One row per product_code x fiscal_year. Use when joining to yearly price/cost/deduction facts to compute revenue/margin. | Use for: yearly revenue = total_sold_quantity * gross_price; compare sales volume by product across years

accepted.name: monthly_sales_by_customer_year
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_code AS customer_code,
  fiscal_year AS fiscal_year,
  SUM(sold_quantity) AS total_sold_quantity
FROM hardware_sales_monthly_clean
GROUP BY customer_code, fiscal_year
accepted.description: Aggregated sold_quantity per customer per fiscal_year. One row per customer_code x fiscal_year. Use for customer-level yearly metrics and applying pre-invoice deductions. | Use for: apply customer-level annual discounts to volumes; customer retention and year-over-year volume change

accepted.name: products_ranked_by_year_sales
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_code AS product_code,
  fiscal_year AS fiscal_year,
  total_sold_quantity AS total_sold_quantity,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY fiscal_year ORDER BY total_sold_quantity DESC) AS sales_rank
FROM monthly_sales_by_product_year
accepted.description: Per-year ranking of products by total sold quantity. One row per product_code x fiscal_year with a rank column (higher volume = rank 1). Useful as a building block for Top-K product queries by year. | Use for: Top N products by year (downstream filter WHERE sales_rank <= N); identify rank/position changes across years

accepted.name: accounts_with_rep_and_region
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.id AS id,
  a.name AS name,
  a.website AS website,
  a.lat AS lat,
  a.long AS long,
  a.primary_poc AS primary_poc,
  a.sales_rep_id AS sales_rep_id,
  r.name AS region_name,
  s.name AS sales_rep_name,
  s.region_id AS sales_rep_region_id
FROM web_accounts AS a
LEFT JOIN web_sales_reps AS s ON a.sales_rep_id = s.id
LEFT JOIN web_region AS r ON s.region_id = r.id
accepted.description: Web accounts enriched with their sales rep name and region name (denormalized account lookup). One row per account id. Useful for CRM analytics joining events/orders to rep/region. | Use for: sales performance by region/rep; geospatial or account-level analysis of events/orders

accepted.name: web_orders_aggregated_by_account_date
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  account_id AS account_id,
  SUBSTR(occurred_at,1,10) AS occurred_date,
  SUM(COALESCE(standard_qty,0)) AS total_standard_qty,
  SUM(COALESCE(gloss_qty,0)) AS total_gloss_qty,
  SUM(COALESCE(poster_qty,0)) AS total_poster_qty,
  SUM(COALESCE(total,0)) AS total_qty,
  SUM(COALESCE(standard_amt_usd,0.0)) AS total_standard_amt_usd,
  SUM(COALESCE(gloss_amt_usd,0.0)) AS total_gloss_amt_usd,
  SUM(COALESCE(poster_amt_usd,0.0)) AS total_poster_amt_usd,
  SUM(COALESCE(total_amt_usd,0.0)) AS total_amt_usd
FROM web_orders
GROUP BY account_id, SUBSTR(occurred_at,1,10)
accepted.description: Aggregate web orders metrics per account per calendar date (date extracted from occurred_at). Preserves account-level daily totals for quantities and amounts. | Use for: account daily order volume and revenue; time series of web orders per account

accepted.name: staffhours_events_with_sequence
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  StaffMember AS StaffMember,
  EventDate AS EventDate,
  EventTime AS EventTime,
  EventType AS EventType,
  LAG(EventType) OVER (PARTITION BY StaffMember ORDER BY EventDate, EventTime) AS prev_event_type,
  LAG(EventDate) OVER (PARTITION BY StaffMember ORDER BY EventDate, EventTime) AS prev_event_date,
  LAG(EventTime) OVER (PARTITION BY StaffMember ORDER BY EventDate, EventTime) AS prev_event_time,
  LEAD(EventType) OVER (PARTITION BY StaffMember ORDER BY EventDate, EventTime) AS next_event_type,
  LEAD(EventDate) OVER (PARTITION BY StaffMember ORDER BY EventDate, EventTime) AS next_event_date,
  LEAD(EventTime) OVER (PARTITION BY StaffMember ORDER BY EventDate, EventTime) AS next_event_time
FROM StaffHours
accepted.description: StaffHours events with previous/next event times per StaffMember ordered by EventDate and EventTime. One row per original event; includes lead/lag to compute durations between Enter/Exit pairs. | Use for: compute staff time-on-site between Enter and Exit; detect missing Enter/Exit pairs or anomalies in event sequences

accepted.name: students_with_enrollment_and_gpa
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.OfferNo AS OfferNo,
  e.StdNo AS StdNo,
  e.EnrGrade AS EnrGrade,
  s.StdFirstName AS StdFirstName,
  s.StdLastName AS StdLastName,
  s.StdCity AS StdCity,
  s.StdState AS StdState,
  s.StdZip AS StdZip,
  s.StdMajor AS StdMajor,
  s.StdClass AS StdClass,
  s.StdGPA AS StdGPA
FROM university_enrollment AS e
LEFT JOIN university_student AS s ON e.StdNo = s.StdNo
accepted.description: Student-level rows joined to their enrollment records and course offerings where available. One row per enrollment (OfferNo, StdNo) preserving student and enrollment keys and the student's GPA (StdGPA). | Use for: student performance in offerings; aggregate grades by course/term/major

accepted.name: offerings_with_faculty
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.OfferNo AS OfferNo,
  o.CourseNo AS CourseNo,
  o.OffTerm AS OffTerm,
  o.OffYear AS OffYear,
  o.OffLocation AS OffLocation,
  o.OffTime AS OffTime,
  o.FacNo AS FacNo,
  o.OffDays AS OffDays,
  f.FacFirstName AS FacFirstName,
  f.FacLastName AS FacLastName,
  f.FacCity AS FacCity,
  f.FacState AS FacState,
  f.FacDept AS FacDept,
  f.FacRank AS FacRank,
  f.FacSalary AS FacSalary
FROM university_offering AS o
LEFT JOIN university_faculty AS f ON o.FacNo = f.FacNo
accepted.description: Course offerings enriched with faculty attributes. One row per OfferNo. Use for term/course-level reporting that needs faculty salary, rank or department. | Use for: faculty workload and pay by offering; course offering rosters and faculty assignments
